latin.242:
Ita verò habet:
Nos Dei Gratia FRIDERICUS REX BORUSSIAE &c. &c.
Salutem & Clementiam nostram!
Admodum Reverende Episcope, Dilecte & Fidelis.
latin.243: Perspectum Tibi est, quò pacto, Nostri praesertim regiminis tempore, pacis inter Evangelicos promovendae summa Nobis cura fuerit, qua etiam, adjuvante Divina Gratia, tantùm profecimus, ut in Regno caeterisque Imperio Nostro subjectis Provinciis publicae illae acerbitates, haeresium imputationes ac mutua Protestantium condemnationes vix ampliùs pro concione audiantur. Unde certa nobis spes affulget, pacifica Nostra consilia, benedicente Deo, felicem fortitura exitum.
latin.244: Cùm verò hinc inde varia, ab utriusque partis Evangelicis, de modo arctioris unionis, vel saltem mutuae majorisque tolerantiae ineundae, consilia typis mandata fuerint, Nosque, tùm publicis ejusmodi scriptis, tùm unanimi omnium desiderio, prae reliquis Principibus, ad manus salutifero huic instaurandae pacis negotio admovendas animati & expergefacti sumus; Collegium Theologorum, ut pacis, ita salutaris intentionis Nostrae, amantium, ad majorem Dei Gloriam Regnique Christi incrementa promovenda, in ipsa Metropoli nostra, erigere clementissimè statuimus; Teque Episcopum Nostrum, Praesidem ejus praesentibus hisce designamus,
latin.245: sequentes Tibi in praesentiarum Assessores adjungentes; nominatim Viros nobis à Concionibus sacris & SS. Theologiae in Academia Nostra Francofurtana Professorem Ordinarium, Samuelem Strimesium, & Danielem Jablonski; nec non Consistorii Nostri Consiliarium & Praepositum Coloniensem, Franciscum Julium Lütkens, nec non Basilicae Magdeburgicae Archidiaconum Winklerum.
latin.246: Tuum itaque, ceu Episcopi, totiusque hujus Consessus Praesidis, erit, nominatos Viros Assessores tuos de clementissima voluntate Nostra, Rescripto hoc declarata, certiores facere, cum iisdem, intra privatos primùm parietes, sine strepitu, convenire ac colloqui, idque agere, ut tùm per colloquia, tùm literas, ad extraneos Theologos dandas, valida media inveniantur, quibus Pax Ecclesiastica, omnibus Protestantium Evangelicorum votis exoptata, si non alibi, in Nostro saltem Regno, Electoratu exterisque terris, procuretur & stabiliatur.
latin.247: Quòd si Tibi Assessoribusque Tuis opus esse videbitur, exteros etiam Theologos Collegio huic vestro ac Conventui adhiberi, eos, praevia tamen clementissima approbatione Nostra, ea, qua par est, humanitate invitabitis, deque omnibus, quae inter vos acta sunt, ad Nos, ore scriptoque referetis. Quò verò in Collegio vel Conventu hoc Charitativo ordinatiùs cuncta consignetur, Secretarium Nostrum Intimum ac Bibliothecarium Fridericum Henricum Ursinum, Proto-Notarium vobis adjungimus, eumque ab ordinario officii nexu quô Bibliotheca Nostra tenetur, durante hoc negotio, clementissimè dispensamus atque absolvimus. Et quemadmodùm nulli dubitamus negotium hocce Irenicum Deo gratissimum fore & Regiam hanc Christianamque intentionem nostram Divina benedictione beatum iri, ita quoque clementissimè confidimus, Vos omnes & singulos, ex vero sinceroque veritatis & pacis studio, curam hanc ac laborem lubentes suscepturos, & omnes nervos intensuros, quò ardentissimi voti Nostri, quod pro pace inter Evangelicos, diu & anxie expetita, stabilienda concepimus, compotes reddamur.
latin.248:
Caeterùm clementia nostra Regia securum Te esse jubemus. Dabantur Coloniae ad Spream d. 25. Martii 1703.
FRIDERICUS REX.
COMES de WARTENBERG, ad Dn. Episcopum Ursinum.
Admodum Reverendo Episcopo nostro Primo, Dilecto & Fideli, Benjamino Ursino.

pass_a.242:
Thus indeed it has:
We by the Grace of God FREDERICK KING OF PRUSSIA etc. etc.
Our Greeting and Clemency!
Most Reverend Bishop, Beloved and Faithful.
pass_a.243: It is clear to You by what means, especially in the time of Our government, the highest care of promoting peace among Evangelicals has been Ours, by which also, with Divine Grace helping, we have so far progressed that in the Kingdom and the other Provinces subject to Our Empire those public bitternesses, imputations of heresies, and mutual condemnations of Protestants are scarcely any longer heard from the pulpit. Whence a sure hope shines upon us that Our pacific counsels, God blessing, will obtain a happy outcome.
pass_a.244: But since here and there various counsels from Evangelicals of either party concerning the manner of entering a closer union, or at least a mutual and greater tolerance, have been committed to print, and We, both by public writings of that kind and by the unanimous desire of all, before the remaining Princes, have been animated and awakened to put hands to this salutary business of restoring peace; we have most clemently determined to erect in our very Metropolis a College of Theologians loving both peace and Our salutary intention, for promoting the greater Glory of God and the increase of Christ’s Kingdom; and by these presents we designate You Our Bishop as its President,
pass_a.245: joining to You for the present the following Assessors; namely Men Ours for sacred Sermons & Ordinary Professor of Sacred Theology in Our Frankfurt Academy, Samuel Strimesius, and Daniel Jablonski; and also Councillor of Our Consistory & Provost of Cölln, Francis Julius Lütkens, and also Archdeacon of the Magdeburg Basilica, Winkler.
pass_a.246: Yours therefore, as Bishop and President of this whole Assembly, will be to make the named Men your Assessors more certain of Our most clement will declared by this Rescript, to meet and colloquy with them first within private walls without noise, and to act so that both by colloquies and by letters to be given to foreign Theologians valid means may be found by which Ecclesiastical Peace, longed for by the vows of all Evangelical Protestants, if not elsewhere, at least in Our Kingdom, Electorate, and other lands, may be procured and established.
pass_a.247: But if it shall seem needful to You and Your Assessors that foreign Theologians also be admitted to this your College and Convention, you will invite them, yet with Our prior most clement approval, with the courtesy that is fitting, and you will report to Us by mouth and writing concerning all things done among you. And so that in this Charitable College or Convention all things may be more orderly recorded, we join to you Our Intimate Secretary and Librarian Frederick Henry Ursinus as Proto-Notary, and during this business most clemently dispense and absolve him from the ordinary bond of office by which Our Library holds him. And just as we doubt not that this Irenical business will be most pleasing to God and that this Our Royal and Christian intention will be blessed with Divine blessing, so also we most clemently trust that You all and each, from true and sincere zeal for truth and peace, will gladly take up this care and labor, and will strain every nerve that we may be made possessors of Our most ardent vow which we have conceived for establishing the peace among Evangelicals long and anxiously desired.
pass_a.248:
For the rest Our Royal clemency bids You be secure. Given at Cölln on the Spree, the 25th of March 1703.
FREDERICK KING.
COUNT of WARTENBERG, to the Lord Bishop Ursinus.
To our Most Reverend First Bishop, Beloved and Faithful, Benjamin Ursinus.

242: We, by God’s grace, Frederick King of Prussia, etc.
Most Reverend Bishop, beloved and faithful.
243: You know how, especially under Our reign, promoting peace among Evangelicals has been Our highest care —

and with God’s grace helping we have come so far that in the Kingdom and Our other subject provinces those public bitternesses, charges of heresy, and Protestants’ mutual condemnations are scarcely heard any longer from the pulpit.
So a sure hope shines on us that Our peace-counsels, God blessing them, will reach a happy end.
244: But since Evangelicals of both sides have here and there put into print various counsels on closer union — or at least on mutual and greater tolerance —
and We, moved by such public writings and by everyone’s unanimous desire ahead of other princes, have been stirred to set hand to this salutary work of restoring peace,
We have most clemently resolved to erect in Our very capital a College of Theologians who love both peace and Our salutary intent, for God’s greater glory and the increase of Christ’s kingdom.
By these presents We name You Our Bishop its President.
245: joining to You for now these Assessors:
Samuel Strimesius, Our man for sacred sermons and Ordinary Professor of Sacred Theology in Our Frankfurt Academy, and Daniel Jablonski;
also Francis Julius Lütkens, councillor of Our Consistory and Provost of Cölln; and Winkler, Archdeacon of the Magdeburg Basilica.
246: Yours, then, as Bishop and President of this whole assembly, will be to make those Assessors sure of Our most clement will declared in this Rescript.
Meet and confer with them first inside private walls, without noise.

See that — by colloquies and by letters to foreign theologians — solid means are found by which the church peace all Evangelical Protestants long for may be procured and settled, if not elsewhere, at least in Our Kingdom, Electorate, and other lands.
247: If You and Your Assessors judge foreign theologians should also be brought into this College and convention, invite them with fitting courtesy — yet only after Our prior most clement approval — and report to Us by word and writing all that is done among you.

And so that everything in this charitable College or convention may be recorded in better order, We join to you Our intimate secretary and librarian Frederick Henry Ursinus as Proto-Notary, and for this business most clemently free him from the ordinary library duty that binds him.

As we do not doubt this irenical work will please God and that Our royal Christian intent will share divine blessing, so we most clemently trust you all, from true zeal for truth and peace, will gladly take up this care and strain every nerve.
Then we may obtain Our most ardent vow — the long, anxiously desired peace among Evangelicals made firm.
248: As for the rest, take security from Our royal clemency.
Issued at Cölln on the Spree, 25 March 1703.
The Count of Wartenberg addresses Lord Bishop Ursinus.
Directed to Benjamin Ursinus, our Most Reverend First Bishop, beloved and faithful.
